findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The nozzle on the horchata refresher was observed soiled. The PIC was made aware. The nozzle was removed, cleaned, and sanitized. Ensure that food contact surfaces are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The. Quaternary ammonia sanitizer in the sani bucket was observed reading between 100-0 ppm. The PIC was notified and the sani bucket was remade. Ensure that the concentration of the sani bucket is routinely checked.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following were observed. 
1. The caulking on the utility sink was observed loose and in a state of disrepair. 
2. The coving tiles on the wall behind the soda syrups and the wall behind he fryers was observed coming off the wall.

Discussed with the PIC. The PIC assured inspector that the relevant repairs will be done. Ensure that the corrective actions for the areas mentioned above are taken.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed  employee not using a barrier to shut the faucet after washing their hands. Discussed with PIC and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff are knowledgeable to used a barrier to shut off the faucet after washing their hands to avoid recontaminating their hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The gasket of the walk-in freezer door is observed in the state of disrepair which is allowing cold air to leave the freezer and for warm air to enter the freezer that may result in ice accumulation. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that a ticket has already been put in for the relevant repairs. Ensure that the gasket is repair to allow the door to seal properly to void ice accumulation and other potential hazards.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: At the start of the inspection, there was a soiled spatula placed behind the faucet of the hand sink. This spatula was removed from this location and placed into the triple sink to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Ensure the hand sink is only used for hand washing.  
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The walk-in freezer door is observed to have an accumulation of ice on the inside of the door. Ensure this ice is removed to allow the door to close properly and to ensure that the surface remains easily cleanable. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The gasket of the walk-in freezer is observed to be in a state of disrepair which is allowing for cold air to leave the freezer and for warm air to enter the freezer resulting in ice accumulation. Ensure once the ice is removed that the door/gasket is repaired to allow the door to seal properly and to maintain the door to be easily cleanable. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: At the start of the inspection, there were no paper towels available at the hand sink. The kitchen employee retrieved paper towels and restocked the paper towel dispenser. Ensure the hand sink is properly stocked with all necessary materials. 
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: There is observed food debris on the floor between the prep tables near the right side of the hood system. PIC stated they will move the table and clean this area. Ensure the physical facilities area cleaned in detail at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11:No sanitizer bucket was present during the start of the inspection. Once inspector informed PIC of issue, a sanitizer bucket was created and measured at a concentration of 200ppm QUAT. Ensure a sanitizer bucket is available during all hours of operation. 
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: The fan in the kitchen, not currently turned on, was observed to have an excessive amount of dust and soil residue. Ensure the fan and fan blades are cleaned before the next use.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed employee sweeping the floor in the kitchen and then immediately attempt to put on gloves for food handling. Employee was stopped, gloves discarded and employee was directed to wash hands, at which time hand washing was very brief (<10 seconds). Employee was educated that proper hand washing is for a full 15-20 seconds and a barrier must be used to turn off faucet so as to not re-contaminate hands. 

2-301.14  (P) Employee did not wash hands after eating/drinking/smoking. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12  (P) Food employee improperly washed hands. Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Reference 2-301.12.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 1) Observed the food prep surfaces in the kitchen to be soiled with food debris. 2) Observed the coffee makers to be soiled black. 3) Observed the plastic collars in the cappuccino machine to be soiled with powder build up. Wash, rinse and sanitize food contact surfaces routinely. After the prep cooler has been cleaned out and repaired, make sure that cutting board and all food prep surfaces are cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Non food contact surface is not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
1) Observed items in the bottom of the prep cooler to be probed at temperatures between 48-52F (capocollo was 48F, cheese was 50F, spinach dip was 48F). The thermometer inside the unit read 55F. No temperature log was available. Ham on the top part of the prep cooler was probed at 33F and ice was observed in the top portion. Service arrived during the inspection to repair. All foods were voluntarily discarded and recorded on their tracking sheet. 

2) Half and half and creamer in the dispenser were probed at 55F. Thermostat on the unit read 53F (thermostat continued to go up to 67 during the inspection). These items were discarded during the inspection and unit was taken out of service until it can be repaired.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly chilled discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed capocollo and tomato based sauce in the prep cooler, and the dairy products such as iced coffee and half and half in the customer service area to not have proper date marking. Observed spinach dip in the prep cooler that was dated 10/17-10/26--this is 10 days rather than the 7 days allowed (this was also out of temperature).  These items were discarded during the inspection and date marking was discussed. 

Tuna salad and egg salad croissants in the reach in cooler were not marked with the date of preparation. These were reported to have been made today and were date marked as such.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
1) Observed the fan in the walk in cooler to have a block of ice on the bottom of the unit that was dripping onto the covered container of pizza dough below. Do not store foods under items that have the potential to contaminate them. 

2)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Foods in the walk in freezer are in open bags in boxes with several of the foods spilling out of the bags. Foods must be held in packaging that prevents the potential for contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: Observed a wet wiping cloth sitting on the counter in the kitchen when not in use. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution in between use.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment: Iced coffee and dairy products in the customer self service area are observed cut straight across. Dispensing tubes must be cut diagonally.
findings.citation_text: 4-502.13  (C) Bulk milk container dispensing tube not properly cut. The bulk milk dispensing tube shall be cut on the diagonal leaving no more than 1 inch protruding from the chilled dispenser. Reference 4-502.13.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: Observed the seal on the right door of the prep cooler at the bottom to be separated from the door. Replace seal as this may not be helping temperature control in this unit.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19  (C) Replace seal (specific piece of equipment) with an corrosion-resistant, nonabsorbent and smooth material meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI certification for use within a foodservice facility.  Reference 4-101.19.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the handles to the hot holding units are soiled with grease and food debris, 2) the fans in the kitchen are soiled with dust, 3) the fans in the walk in freezer are soiled with dust, 4) the drip pans on the beverages dispensers in the customer service area are soiled with buildup, 5) the hand washing sink in the kitchen soiled.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Floors are observed soiled with food debris in the kitchen and the walk in freezer. Clean the floors.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the coffee maker spouts to be soiled black. Wash, rinse and sanitize spouts.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the handles to the hot holding cases on the kitchen side with grease, 2) the cabinet underneath the soda fountain to be soiled with water and mold. Clean these non-food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.comment:

750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.citation_text: 750.1160 Observed penetration of the outer wall around a vent. Potential entrances for rodents and insects are prohibited. Repair the vent.

findings.citation_text: 750.800 Soiled cabinets under the soda station. Non-food contact surfaces must be kept clean. Clean non food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed the following with a past date mark: spinach 11/21, roast beef 11/17, and turkey 11/17. All items were immediately discarded to CORRECT the violation. 
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed multiple gaskets peeling off on the reach in cooler holding energy drinks and Dr. Pepper. Repair or replace gaskets.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:

750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.comment: Violation 3a still remains per original inpsection. Repair cooler. Bottom portion of cooler 48-50F.

Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

Metal insert of sink at mens restroom is broken. Repair sink.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

Under 3 compartment sink there is stand water underneath the plexiglass on top of the grease trap. Repair flooring/grease trap to not retain water.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
1) Caulk at the hand sink in the kitchen is moldy. Recaulk sink. 2) Mold on the walll to the left of the walk in cooler door. Clean wall. 3) Mens restroom sink, wall juncture is craked. Repair wall.

750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.comment:

750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similiar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
The walls around the mop sink were soiled.

Clean the walls around the mop sink.

Quat sanitizer is typically used but bleach is also available for use. Obtain and use both quat and chlorine test kits to ensure proper concentrations of sanitizer solutions. A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) spout of coffee maker (buildup) & B) plastic organizers in walkin cooler used for food storage. Properly clean and sanitize the above items and all food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

Clean the above items and all non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris - including inside cabinets and drawers and shelves/drink organizers in coolers.

findings.citation_text: 750.1120 - Handsink across from ice machine was soiled. Clean the handsinks and all related fixtures daily/as needed and maintain them clean.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) Coving was loose or missing in the following areas: 1) (R) under men's room handsink; 2) (R) in room with ice machine (loose behind the ice machine/missing in other locations throughout the room); 3) (R) under the bulletin board in the laundry area; 4) under prep table in kitchen; & 5) women's room (wall by the door). Repair or replace all missing coving. In some areas caulk may be used if that is easier to seal the floor to wall joint. B) Floors were observed to be soiled in the walkin freezer, in the walkin cooler (along reach-in section), and under the prep table in the kitchen. Clean floors daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris. (see general comments)

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text: 750.1320 - Spray bottle labeled bleach water was at a concentration much higher than 100ppm chlorine. The inspector's test strip turned white with a black edge, which indicates the solution consisted of mostly bleach. When water was added to the solution it was still too strong - test strips turned dark purple to black. Solution was dumped out to be remade. Maintain concentration of bleach solutions at 100ppm chlorine for sanitizing general surfaces and clean in place food contact surfaces. A separate solution should be made/used for bathroom floors if you wish to have a stronger bleach solution for mopping purposes. Poisonous/toxic substances must be used properly so as not to contaminate surfaces or pose a hazard to people.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text: 750.130 - Packages of raw bacon were next to/touching packages of hotdogs on the bottom shelf in the cooler by the self service drink counter. All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or away from raw foods. Bacon was moved to the far end of the bottom shelf away from the hotdogs.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Boxes of food were observed on the floor in the walkin freezer. Foods shall be protected at all times. Store foods elevated off the floor at least 6 inches.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text: 750.690 - A) (R) Edges of shelves by kitchen handsink were in worn/rough. B) Edge inside trash cabinet below cappuccino machine was worn/rough. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition. Repair or replace the shelves so they are smooth and cleanable.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - Wet wiping cloths were observed on the prep table and by the fryer. Wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution between uses to inhibit the growth of microorganisms. Employee made a bucket of sanitizer during the inspection for the rags. **Use test strips to verify proper concentration of sanitizer buckets & in the 3 part sink when doing dishes - concentration = 200ppm quat**

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - Drip guard of the ice machine had some buildup on it, and the top inside the microwave had dried food debris on it. Properly clean and sanitize these items and all food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris and prevent cross contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) counter under cappuccino machine; B) drawer below microwave; C) shelf holding microwave; D) black organizers at drink counter; & E) soda syrup box rack by kitchen handsink. Clean the above items and all non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.citation_text: 750.1120 - Handsink across from ice machine was blocked by the ice bag stand. When the stand was moved by the inspector it was possible to see the handsink was soiled because the bottom of the stand was dirty. Handsinks must be accessible at all times to allow for proper handwashing. Do not block handsinks, and keep the handsinks clean.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text: 750.1120 - A) (R) Paper towels were not available at the handsink across from the ice machine. B) Both handsinks were observed to be soiled - inside basin of sink across from ice machine and faucet of sink in kitchen. Provide an adequate supply of soap and paper towels at all handsinks to allow for proper handwashing. Keep handsinks clean to prevent potential cross contamination of hands during the handwashing process.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) Floors were under shelves in the store, by the ice machine in the corner/along the wall, and in the walkin cooler along the wall below the reach-in doors (especially under milk section). Floors shall be keep clean. Clean the floors in these areas. B) Coving was observed pulling away from the walls or missing in the men's room under the handsink, in the room with the ice machine, by the mopsink, under the 3 part sink, and under the bulletin board in the laundry area. Floor to wall junctures shall be properly sealed. Repair/replace the coving in the above areas and any other locations throughout the store that may be in disrepair.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed previously heated sausage gravy at 57F, without a label.  Gravy was discarded.  This is a medium risk facility.  Do not keep heated food for re-service.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 140°F or above)

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed an open bottle of Vitamin Water in the prep cooler above cheese and salami.  Do not store employee food with food for the establishment.  Bottle was discarded.
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed a container of pizza to go boxes on the floor in the storage room.  Store at least six inches above the floor.
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the edges of three shelves next to the hand sink to be worn at the edges.  Repair the edges so they are smooth, durable and non-absorbant or replace.
750-600 Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily cleanable

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed a build-up of coffee at the coffemaker water spout and mildew on the inside ledge of the ice maker.  Clean and sanitize the spout and ice machine and maintain clean.
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed an old spill in the cabinet under the pop machine.  Clean the cabinet.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Did not observe soap at the hand sink in the kitchen and towels at the hand sink by the ice maker.
750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.
